content.summary: Retrospective on git-review-ui: full /changes route with file navigation, stage-aware diffs, line comments, and submit-to-prompt

outcome.learning_milestone: User can /changes → navigate → diff → comment → submit-to-prompt end-to-end
outcome.delta: ~9x faster than plan estimate due to orchestrated parallelism and focused work items

surprises: Commit plan scope initially narrower than explore findings — orchestrator post-commit review caught 3 misalignments before build started
WI-04 (diff pane) required server-side /file/content extension and SDK regeneration — 8 files changed vs expected 2-3 for a 'UI component'
<diff> opentui element confirmed no line-level interaction API — the pre-identified risk materialized and the planned fallback (DialogPrompt line selection) worked smoothly
Wall-clock time was ~9x faster than estimate — parallelized build waves and specific acceptance criteria enabled autonomous builder completion without clarification rounds

worked.pattern: Parallel explore probes with different focus areas
worked.why: Dispatching codebase feasibility + upstream PR analysis in parallel gave rich decision surface in minutes and caught opentui#621 dependency risk before any code was written
worked.example: Explorer 1 mapped File.status/File.read/diff rendering. Explorer 2 analyzed anomalyco/opencode#12188 and opentui#621 dependency.

worked.pattern: Orchestrator post-commit review against explore context
worked.why: Catches scope drift between explore findings and committed plan before expensive build phase
worked.example: Orchestrator found commit plan deferred directory grouping, staged diffs, and had auto-send vs append-to-prompt wrong — all corrected before build started

worked.why: Maximizes throughput while preventing cross-file merge conflicts. Compressed 6 sequential items into 4 effective build steps.
worked.example: Wave 1: WI-01+WI-02 (independent). Serial: WI-03. Wave 2: WI-04+WI-05 (orthogonal UI slices). Serial: WI-06 (integrator).

worked.pattern: Additive optional schema fields for backward compatibility
worked.why: Adding optional stage field to File.Info meant zero breakage for existing consumers. No migration, no feature flags.
worked.example: stage: z.enum(['staged','unstaged','untracked']).optional() — existing callers just ignore it

worked.pattern: Pure formatting functions as testable islands
worked.why: format-comments.ts was naturally testable because it's pure. It attracted the only unit test in the feature and the review specifically requested more coverage for it.
worked.example: format-comments.ts: Comment[] → string, tested in changes-format-comments.test.ts

worked.pattern: Explicit acceptance criteria with mandatory typecheck gate
worked.why: Every work item required 'bun run typecheck passes' — this caught integration errors at each step. 100% criteria met without builder needing clarification.
worked.example: 56 acceptance criteria across 6 items, all marked [x] with validation notes

worked.pattern: Holistic review for integrated feature sets
worked.why: Reviewing all 6 items as a batch caught cross-cutting issues (sequential git commands, what/how braid) that per-item review would miss
worked.example: Review found: parallel git commands, conditional diff fetch, client-side diff synthesis — all cross-item concerns

worked.pattern: ReturnTo route pattern for stateless navigation
worked.why: Simple field on route type solves back-navigation without a history stack or persistent state

didnt_work.anti_pattern: Commit plan scope narrower than explore findings
didnt_work.why: Different agents (explorer vs commitment-analyst) can have different interpretations of scope. The commit plan deferred items the explore phase identified as requirements.
didnt_work.example: Directory grouping and staged diff viewing deferred in plan but identified as user requirements in explore

didnt_work.anti_pattern: Underestimating server-side plumbing for 'UI' work items
didnt_work.why: WI-04 was titled 'Build the diff viewing pane' but required extending /file/content query schema, modifying File.read(), and regenerating SDK
didnt_work.example: 8 files changed including server route, file module, SDK gen types — the 'UI component' touched 3 backend layers

didnt_work.anti_pattern: No tests on 5 of 6 work items
didnt_work.why: Acceptance criteria only required typecheck, so builders didn't add tests. Review flagged missing coverage.
didnt_work.example: tests: not_run on WI-01 through WI-05. Only WI-06 had a test because it had an extractable pure function.

didnt_work.anti_pattern: Client-side diff synthesis in UI component
didnt_work.why: makeDiff() in diff-pane.tsx mixes rendering with data transformation — a what/how braid
didnt_work.example: DiffPane creates synthetic diffs for added/untracked files instead of receiving them from backend

didnt_work.anti_pattern: Sequential subprocess calls shipped without parallelization
didnt_work.why: 5 independent git commands run sequentially in File.status() — known latency issue deferred for speed of delivery
didnt_work.example: git diff --cached, git diff, git ls-files, git diff --name-only (x2) all await sequentially

heuristics: When explore and commit are done by different agents, always have the orchestrator validate commit scope against explore findings before approving build start
When a work item title says 'UI component' but the diff pane needs data the backend doesn't provide yet, scope the server changes into the same work item — don't pretend it's UI-only
When parallelizing build waves, the dependency graph determines maximum safe parallelism — never parallelize items that touch the same files
For data model enrichments, always prefer additive optional fields over breaking changes — zero migration cost, zero rollback risk
Include 'unit test for pure functions' in acceptance criteria, not just typecheck — typecheck doesn't catch logic bugs
When an explore phase identifies a risk with a known fallback, document both in the work item — builders can execute the fallback immediately without re-exploring
Holistic review beats per-item review for features with shared state or cross-cutting concerns
Wall-clock estimates for orchestrated parallel builds should be 3-5x lower than serial estimates — parallelism + focused scope dramatically compresses cycle time

explore_phase: Parallel probes with different focus areas (codebase feasibility + external prior art) produce higher-quality option ranking than sequential exploration
When upstream PRs exist, always dispatch a dedicated probe to evaluate reuse potential and dependency risks
commit_phase: After commit-plan is generated, validate scope against explore options before approving build — different agents can interpret scope differently
For UI features requiring new data, include server-side plumbing in the same work item as the component that consumes it — don't split across items unless the server change has independent value
build_phase: Safe parallelism = items that don't touch the same files. Two build waves with 2 parallel items each compressed 6 items from ~10h serial to ~1h wall-clock.
Include 'unit test for pure functions' in acceptance criteria — pure functions are the highest-ROI test targets and builders will write them if asked
review_phase: For integrated features (3+ work items sharing state/files), use holistic review, not per-item review
Non-blocking review findings should generate follow-up backlog items automatically to ensure they're tracked
